name: USA

complexity.notes: Aerospace, pharma, semis, aircraft, medical devices — few peers. Some commodity creep in petroleum exports.

sovereignty.notes: Full nuclear sovereignty, domestic jet engines (GE/P&W), ITAR control over others' systems. Institutional procurement speed is the binding constraint.

key_signal: The world's deepest complexity-sovereignty stack — until you look at the joints. F-35 software routes through American infrastructure that allies are actively designing around, and the Replicator autonomous systems program failed its own fielding test. The binding constraint isn't capability; it's institutional speed. The gap between what the US can imagine and what it can procure and deploy is itself a strategic vulnerability.

name: France

complexity.notes: Aerospace, luxury, pharma, nuclear systems, Airbus — genuinely high complexity basket.

sovereignty.notes: Independent nuclear deterrent, SNECMA M88 domestic engine, arms exports without US permission. FCAS collapse leaves France as sole engine of European aerospace sovereignty.

key_signal: The only NATO member outside the US with a genuinely independent nuclear deterrent, a domestic fighter engine, and arms export authority unconstrained by Washington. FCAS collapse makes France the sole engine of European aerospace sovereignty — winner of a competition it didn't enter. The FCAS void is France's opportunity and its burden simultaneously.

name: Germany

complexity.notes: Precision machinery, advanced chemicals, automotive systems — among the most complex export baskets globally.

sovereignty.notes: No nuclear deterrent, no domestic jet engine, FCAS cancelled after nine years and zero prototypes. Zeitenwende was a political declaration.

key_signal: The most extreme gap in the cohort. FCAS cancelled at ILA Berlin after nine years and zero prototypes. Germany now faces a binary choice: GCAP partnership or deeper F-35 dependency, with no third option. Zeitenwende was a political declaration. The factory floors haven't moved. The sovereignty score remains 3.

name: South Korea

complexity.notes: Semiconductors (HBM/DRAM), ships, EVs, displays — rapidly ascending complexity. Samsung and SK Hynix produce 90% of global HBM.

sovereignty.notes: KF-21 uses GE engine, no nuclear deterrent, US security umbrella. HBM chip dominance gives structural position in next-generation paradigm.

key_signal: Samsung and SK Hynix produce 90 percent of global high-bandwidth memory — the chip architecture autonomous systems actually run on — giving Korea structural position in the next-generation paradigm its sovereignty score undersells. The binding constraint is the US security umbrella: the KF-21 uses a GE engine, no nuclear deterrent exists, and the entire defense posture assumes American presence. The chip dominance is real. The sovereignty architecture beneath it is borrowed.

name: China

complexity.notes: Electronics, EVs, machinery — ascending fast. ASML lithography dependence and quality gaps in high-end manufacturing hold complexity to 7.

sovereignty.notes: Domestic engines (WS-10/WS-15), independent nuclear deterrent, combat-demonstrated autonomous swarms, arms sales unconstrained. Most complete sovereignty architecture in the dataset.

key_signal: The most dangerous asymmetry in the cohort, running opposite to Germany. Sovereignty architecture nearly complete — domestic engines, independent nuclear deterrent, combat-demonstrated autonomous swarms, arms sales to anyone. Complexity held to 7 by continued ASML lithography dependence and persistent quality gaps in high-end manufacturing. The trajectory is unambiguous: complexity rising faster than any other nation in the dataset.

name: Russia

complexity.notes: Crude oil, refined petroleum, natural gas, coal, gold — 60% hydrocarbon concentration. Dutch Disease fully expressed.

sovereignty.notes: Domestic engines (AL-41), independent nuclear deterrent, total software sovereignty, combat-deployed autonomous systems. No foreign partner dependencies.

key_signal: The defining case for why the binding constraint matters more than any individual score. Every hard sovereignty attribute — domestic engines, independent nuclear deterrent, combat-deployed autonomous systems, total software sovereignty — sitting on an export basket that is 60 percent hydrocarbons. Remove the oil price and the military apparatus has no economic foundation to sustain itself. A formidable weapon that cannot be reloaded.

name: Netherlands

complexity.notes: ASML (sole EUV lithography manufacturer), chemicals, pharma — complexity overstated by transit trade through Rotterdam.

sovereignty.notes: No nuclear, no domestic engine. F-35 sovereignty concerns reached parliament. ASML operates under Dutch-American export control jointly.

key_signal: ASML is arguably the most strategically important company in the world — the sole manufacturer of EUV lithography machines without which no nation can produce leading-edge semiconductors. That chokepoint gives the Netherlands structural leverage that its sovereignty score cannot capture. But ASML operates under Dutch-American export control jointly, and the defense posture is entirely NATO-dependent. Enormous latent power, almost no sovereign architecture to wield it.

name: Belgium

complexity.notes: Chemicals, pharma, processed diamonds, food — mid-complexity. Transit hub status distorts numbers.

sovereignty.notes: Hosts NATO headquarters while maintaining one of the alliance's lowest defense industrial footprints. No doctrine, no engine, no autonomous systems program.

key_signal: A mid-complexity economy with no meaningful military sovereignty. Hosts NATO headquarters while maintaining one of the alliance's lowest defense industrial footprints. No autonomous systems program, no edge chip capability, no doctrine of sovereignty. Full client-state posture by every measure in this framework.

name: Canada

complexity.notes: Oil, autos (assembled not designed), lumber, gold — resource-heavy with manufacturing dependency. Best-educated Canadians build things in California.

sovereignty.notes: No nuclear, no domestic engine. F-35 procurement paralysis for years over software sovereignty concerns — then bought it anyway. NORAD dependency on US.

key_signal: The F-35 procurement saga is the clearest demonstration of sovereignty anxiety in practice. Canada spent years paralyzed over a militarily straightforward decision because locking into US-controlled software infrastructure felt politically untenable — then bought the F-35 anyway. Oil and lumber dominate the export basket. The best-educated Canadians build things in California. The binding constraint of 1 is structural, not incidental.

name: Finland

complexity.notes: Machinery, electronics, paper — Nokia legacy; ascending industrial base. Small export basket but high value.

sovereignty.notes: Joined NATO 2023, immediately bought F-35s. Consistent defense doctrine across governments driven by Russian threat on border.

key_signal: Joined NATO in 2023 and immediately bought F-35s — rational strategically, but permanently embedded a foreign software dependency into its primary air sovereignty platform. Consistent defense doctrine across governments, driven by the Russian threat on its border. The autonomous systems and edge chip scores are near-zero. A small nation that chose alliance integration over sovereign architecture, deliberately and not unreasonably.

name: Poland

complexity.notes: Machinery, furniture, autos (assembled), food — ascending complexity via K2PL and SAFE investments. Score rising.

sovereignty.notes: No nuclear, no engine. K2PL factory, drone armada partnership with Ukraine, SAFE loans executing. Sovereignty architecture under construction.

key_signal: The sovereignty score today understates where Poland is going. The K2PL factory at Bumar-Łabędy, the drone armada partnership with Ukraine, the SAFE loan execution, and the elevation of South Korea to second-most-important ally are foundations of a defense industrial civilization being built on a deliberate timeline. Poland scores 2 now. The structural work underway suggests it scores materially higher in five years. Watch the gap narrow.

name: Ukraine

complexity.notes: Grain, sunflower oil, iron ore — commodity base. Ivchenko engine tradition is the exception. Pre-war basket snapshot.

sovereignty.notes: Combat-validated GPS-denied autonomous systems, weekly iteration cycles, Brave1 pipeline. Sovereign software update cycle. No nuclear deterrent (surrendered 1994).

key_signal: The most analytically unusual entry. The complexity score reflects the pre-war export basket — grain, sunflower oil, iron ore — genuinely low-complexity. The sovereignty score reflects a nation building new forms of sovereignty in real time, under fire. Combat-validated GPS-denied autonomous systems, weekly iteration cycles, Brave1 as a structured pipeline — Ukraine is generating defense IP that no other nation in this dataset produces from operational experience. The binding constraint of 3 is a snapshot of an economy at war. The trajectory is the story.

name: Brazil

complexity.notes: Soybeans, iron ore, crude oil, sugar, meat — high commodity concentration. Embraer is the outlier that proves the rule.

sovereignty.notes: No nuclear deterrent, no domestic fighter engine. No consistent sovereignty doctrine across governments. No autonomous systems program.

key_signal: Embraer is a genuine outlier — a world-class regional aircraft manufacturer that demonstrates Brazil has the industrial DNA for high-complexity production. The problem is that Embraer is surrounded by soybeans, iron ore, and crude oil. No consistent sovereignty doctrine exists across governments. No autonomous systems program. No edge chip capability. Embraer proves Brazil could build a different economy. The rest of the export basket proves it hasn't.

name: Turkiye

complexity.notes: Autos, machinery, textiles, steel — mid-complexity. Bayraktar is genuine uplift. Ascending trajectory.

sovereignty.notes: Baykar K2/Sivrisinek/Mızrak GPS-denied autonomous operation demonstrated. KARGU combat deployed. TB2 in 34 countries. Engine independence unmet.

key_signal: The most interesting Tier 2 entry and the clearest upward trajectory outside Poland and Ukraine. Baykar's K2, Sivrisinek, and Mızrak drones now demonstrate GPS-denied autonomous operation. KARGU has combat deployment. Arms exports at 95 percent of Baykar revenue. TB2 in 34 countries. The engine independence ambition remains unmet, but the autonomous systems trajectory is genuine and accelerating. Turkey is building sovereignty from the drone tier up — precisely the direction the framework's own logic says matters next.

name: UK

complexity.notes: Aerospace, pharma, financial services, machinery, precision manufacturing — genuinely high complexity, services-heavy but high-value.

sovereignty.notes: Rolls-Royce domestic engines, independent nuclear deterrent, GCAP leadership, arms exports without US permission, consistent doctrine surviving Brexit.

key_signal: The most coherent NATO sovereignty story outside the US and France. Rolls-Royce domestic engines, independent nuclear deterrent, GCAP leadership, arms exports without Washington's permission, and a consistent defense industrial doctrine that survived Brexit without strategic incoherence. GCAP is led by BAE Systems while FCAS collapses under Franco-German governance failure. The absence of domestic edge chip capability is the binding constraint's only soft joint.

name: Italy

complexity.notes: Industrial machinery, pharma, premium vehicles, food, chemicals. Leonardo and ITP Aero are real.

sovereignty.notes: Leonardo and F-35 FACO at Cameri give genuine depth. GCAP partnership. No nuclear deterrent, no domestic engine, inconsistent doctrine across governments.

key_signal: Leonardo and the F-35 FACO facility at Cameri give Italy genuine defense industrial depth that its GDP ranking undersells. GCAP puts Italy at the center of the only fully operational Western sixth-generation program — and FCAS's collapse makes that position significantly more valuable overnight. No nuclear deterrent, no domestic engine, and inconsistent doctrine across governments hold the sovereignty score at 3.

name: Spain

complexity.notes: Vehicles, refined petroleum, food, pharma, machinery — mid-complexity. Airbus Military and Indra are genuine but basket leans commodity.

sovereignty.notes: FCAS cancelled after nine years and zero prototypes. Stranded without carrier jet program after abandoning F-35B. Indra radar systems are the only sovereignty asset.

key_signal: FCAS cancellation at ILA Berlin defines this score. Spain spent nine years and billions on a sixth-generation fighter program that produced zero prototypes, leaving it stranded without a carrier jet program after abandoning the F-35B. Indra's radar systems and Airbus Military provide a mid-tier industrial base. The sovereignty architecture is a client-state posture with the client relationship now uncertain. The binding constraint of 1 is a fresh wound, not a chronic condition.

name: Norway

complexity.notes: Petroleum gases, crude oil, fish, aluminum, machinery — resource-heavy but KONGSBERG is the meaningful outlier. Sovereign wealth fund is the Dutch Disease inoculation.

sovereignty.notes: KONGSBERG NSM and JSM sought by allies without conditions. Consistent doctrine across governments. F-35 buyer with no domestic engine.

key_signal: The most sophisticated Dutch Disease inoculation ever attempted — the sovereign wealth fund as a deliberate structural hedge against resource dependency. KONGSBERG is the sovereignty story: NSM and JSM missiles are the Western anti-ship missile of choice, sought by allies without conditions. Consistent defense industrial doctrine across governments is rarer than it looks. The binding constraint is the export basket: petroleum gases and crude oil still dominate, and the complexity score cannot escape that gravity however elegant the hedge.

name: Denmark

complexity.notes: Pharmaceuticals (Novo Nordisk dominates), medication mixes, blood fractions — genuinely high-complexity exports. Vestas wind, Maersk logistics.

sovereignty.notes: F-35 trap in its purest form. TR-3 failure grounded Danish operational readiness. Recalled aircraft from Luke AFB to maintain pilot training continuity.

key_signal: Novo Nordisk alone accounts for a disproportionate share of Danish GDP — medication mixes and blood fractions are among the highest-complexity exports any country produces. The complexity score is genuine. The sovereignty score reflects the F-35 trap in its purest form: TR-3 failure grounded Danish operational readiness, Denmark recalled aircraft from Luke Air Force Base to maintain pilot training continuity. A high-complexity economy in a zero-sovereignty defense posture.

name: Sweden

complexity.notes: Autos (Volvo/Scania), machinery, pharma, telecom (Ericsson), defense systems (Saab) — genuinely high complexity. ITAR-free defense architecture is itself a complexity product.

sovereignty.notes: Gripen E flies Volvo Aero RM12 domestic engine. Sells globally without ITAR constraints by explicit design. A26 submarine, LUUV program. Consistent doctrine across 40+ years of governments.

key_signal: The most underrated sovereignty score in the dataset — and the one most directly relevant to the KUSP argument. The Gripen flies a domestic Volvo Aero engine. Saab sells globally without ITAR constraints by explicit design. The A26 submarine and LUUV program anchor the autonomous undersea tier. The doctrine of open-architecture sovereignty has held across Social Democrat and conservative governments for four decades. Sweden is building the software spine of a new defense paradigm without anyone fully noticing.

name: Japan

complexity.notes: Highest ECI score in the dataset. Cars, precision machinery, electronics, robotics, optical instruments — the most complex export basket on earth.

sovereignty.notes: Yoshida Doctrine unwinding under Takaichi doctrine. GCAP partner. XF9 engine prototype exists. Article 9 reinterpretation the permission structure. No nuclear deterrent.

key_signal: The highest ECI score in the dataset — the most complex export basket on earth. The Yoshida Doctrine's 70-year legacy of trading military autonomy for economic growth is now actively unwinding under the Takaichi doctrine. GCAP is the sovereignty bet, the XF9 engine prototype the signal, the Article 9 reinterpretation the permission structure. Japan is not building sovereignty from scratch — it is unlocking it. The gap will narrow faster than any other nation in the dataset except possibly Poland.

name: India

complexity.notes: Refined petroleum, pharmaceuticals, machinery, textiles, gems — ascending but still mid-complexity. IT sector is services not goods exports.

sovereignty.notes: Independent nuclear deterrent. Tejas uses GE F404 operationally while Kaveri domestic engine stalls. BrahMos exports growing. Most deliberate non-alignment in the dataset.

key_signal: The most deliberate non-alignment in the dataset. Russian engines, French fighters, American drones, Israeli systems, domestic missile program — every procurement decision optimizes for avoiding dependency on any single partner. The Tejas uses a GE engine operationally while the Kaveri domestic engine program stalls. The binding constraint of 5 reflects genuine military sovereignty — independent nuclear deterrent, credible without any alliance — but complexity held down by an economy that still exports more refined petroleum than software. The gap of zero is the most honest number in the dataset: India is precisely as sovereign as it is complex.

name: Israel

complexity.notes: Defense technology, diamonds, pharma, precision optical instruments, medical devices. Defense exports at record $14.8 billion.

sovereignty.notes: Unacknowledged nuclear deterrent fully sovereign. Record defense exports while fighting multi-front war. Arrow 3 in Germany. Iron Beam operational December 2025. Autonomous ground vehicles in combat.

key_signal: The second-highest sovereignty score in the dataset — earned, not inherited. Record $14.8 billion in defense exports while fighting a multi-front war. Arrow 3 batteries in Germany. Iron Beam operational December 2025. Autonomous ground vehicles in combat in Gaza. Others seek Israeli technology at scale. The nuclear deterrent is unacknowledged and fully sovereign. The binding constraint is complexity — diamonds and defense technology are genuine but a narrow basket.

name: Taiwan

complexity.notes: Semiconductors are 65% of exports. TSMC at 64% global foundry market share, 90%+ of leading-edge capacity. Most concentrated high-complexity export in the dataset.

sovereignty.notes: No nuclear deterrent. US approval required on most defense exports. TSMC is Q9 answered most completely of any nation. Existential alliance dependency.

key_signal: TSMC at 64 percent global foundry market share, 90 percent of leading-edge capacity. Q9 — does your country design and manufacture the semiconductor architectures that matter for autonomous systems at the tactical edge — is the question Taiwan answers most completely of any nation on earth. The gap of 4 is the framework's most pointed geopolitical observation: Taiwan produces the chip that defines the next military paradigm and cannot defend itself without the nation that most needs that chip.

name: Australia

complexity.notes: Iron ore, coal, natural gas, gold, beef — among the most resource-concentrated baskets in the dataset for a wealthy nation. Cochlear and CSL are outliers.

sovereignty.notes: AUKUS is the sovereignty ambition and the sovereignty confession simultaneously. No nuclear deterrent. F-35 software dependency. First SSN-AUKUS not until early 2040s.

key_signal: AUKUS is simultaneously Australia's sovereignty ambition and its sovereignty confession. The agreement explicitly acknowledges that Australia cannot defend itself without the US and UK, while beginning the 20-year process of building the capability to try. Iron ore, coal, and LNG dominate the export basket. The first SSN-AUKUS doesn't arrive until the early 2040s. The binding constraint of 1 will remain 1 for the better part of a generation.

name: Iran

complexity.notes: Crude oil, petroleum gases, petrochemicals, pistachio nuts, methanol — extreme hydrocarbon concentration. Sanctions prevented meaningful complexity development.

sovereignty.notes: Shahed swarms combat-deployed across two theaters. GPS-denied terminal guidance demonstrated at scale. 45 years of consistent revolutionary doctrine. Total software sovereignty by necessity.

key_signal: The most extreme sovereignty-without-complexity case after North Korea. Sanctions-forged self-reliance produced a defense industrial base that fights at well above its economic weight — Shahed swarms combat-deployed across two theaters, GPS-denied terminal guidance demonstrated at scale, 45 years of consistent revolutionary doctrine. But the export basket is crude oil and petrochemicals under sanctions. The binding constraint is an economy that isolation has kept permanently pre-industrial.

name: North Korea

complexity.notes: Weapons and ammunition, coal, textiles — the most constrained export basket in the dataset. Sanctions and isolation produced near-total commodity dependence.

sovereignty.notes: Nuclear deterrent fully sovereign. Arms exported to Russia at volumes exceeding Russian domestic production. Total software sovereignty by design. Juche self-reliance doctrine across three Kim generations.

key_signal: The extreme case the framework was built to identify — a sovereign military apparatus sitting on a non-economy. Nuclear deterrent fully sovereign. Arms exported to Russia at volumes exceeding Russian domestic production. Total software sovereignty by design and isolation. The binding constraint of 1 represents the most complete separation of military sovereignty from economic complexity in the dataset. Juche as defense doctrine; starvation as complexity policy.

name: Pakistan

complexity.notes: Textiles, rice, leather goods, surgical instruments, cement — low complexity. JF-17 is the outlier in an otherwise commodity-heavy basket.

sovereignty.notes: Nuclear deterrent fully sovereign. JF-17 domestic airframe with Chinese WS-13 engine. No consistent doctrine across governments. Genuine hard sovereignty attributes.

key_signal: The nuclear deterrent is real and fully sovereign — the clearest defense sovereignty signal in South Asia. The JF-17 flies a Chinese engine, which is the Pakistani analog to South Korea's KF-21 situation, but with less industrial base beneath it. No consistent doctrine across governments. The binding constraint of 3 reflects a country that has genuine hard sovereignty attributes and almost no economic complexity to sustain them.

name: Saudi Arabia

complexity.notes: Crude oil, refined petroleum, petrochemicals, plastics, fertilizers — 70-74% hydrocarbons. Vision 2030 localization at 19.35% after six years.

sovereignty.notes: No nuclear deterrent. F-15, Typhoon, F-35 buyer. $80 billion defense budget spent almost entirely on foreign procurement. US security guarantee is existential.

key_signal: The most complete Dutch Disease case in the dataset. Seventy to seventy-four percent hydrocarbon exports, $80 billion annual defense budget spent almost entirely on foreign procurement, Vision 2030 localization at 19.35 percent after six years of effort. The framework's Dutch Disease diagnostic produces its clearest answer here: if oil disappeared tomorrow, Saudi Arabia has no industrial alternative. The binding constraint and complexity score tell the same story.

name: UAE

complexity.notes: Crude oil, refined petroleum, gold re-exports, aluminum, plastics — mid-commodity. EDGE Group is a genuine and rapidly ascending outlier.

sovereignty.notes: EDGE Group founded 2019, defense exports tripling. Anduril joint venture. NATO members buying Caracal rifles. One government — Q6 fails. Ascending trajectory.

key_signal: The most interesting ascending case in the contested cohort. EDGE Group founded 2019, defense exports tripling, Anduril joint venture for autonomous systems, NATO members buying Caracal rifles. The UAE is building a defense industrial base faster than any comparable nation in its GDP tier. The binding constraint of 4 is today's score. If EDGE's trajectory holds across three governments — the Q6 question it currently fails — this score moves materially.

name: Belarus

complexity.notes: Potash, refined petroleum products, tractors, chemical products, machinery — resource and Soviet-era industrial base. No meaningful independent complexity development.

sovereignty.notes: After 2020, Lukashenko traded every remaining sovereignty attribute for Russian protection. Nuclear weapons on Belarusian soil are Russian-controlled. Not a country with low sovereignty — a territory with Russian sovereignty.

key_signal: The most complete sovereignty abdication in the dataset. After 2020, Lukashenko traded every remaining attribute of Belarusian sovereignty for Russian protection of his regime. Nuclear weapons on Belarusian soil are Russian-controlled. Defense procurement is Russian-supplied. The software on Belarusian military systems is Russian-operated. Belarus is not a country with low sovereignty — it is a territory with Russian sovereignty exercised through a local administrator.

name: Serbia

complexity.notes: Machinery, electrical equipment, vehicles, fruits, base metals — mid-complexity for the region. Zastava arms tradition and some aerospace components are genuine.

sovereignty.notes: HQ-22 Chinese air defense alongside Russian MiG-29s alongside EU candidate status. Consistent multi-vector hedging doctrine. Zastava arms exports without major partner approval.

key_signal: The most deliberate hedger in the European cohort. HQ-22 Chinese air defense alongside Russian MiG-29s alongside EU candidate status — the multi-vector doctrine is consistent across governments even if the content shifts. Zastava arms exports provide partial credit. The binding constraint of 2 reflects a mid-complexity economy that has chosen strategic ambiguity as its sovereignty doctrine, which is a doctrine, not an absence of one.

name: Indonesia

complexity.notes: Coal, palm oil, iron and steel, nickel, mineral fuels — extreme commodity concentration. Nickel ore export ban is an attempt at downstream complexity building.

sovereignty.notes: Buying simultaneously from US, South Korea, France, Turkey, Netherlands, Brazil — multi-dependency not non-alignment. KF-21 partnership payments fell into arrears. No consistent doctrine.

key_signal: The largest archipelagic nation on earth with a defense procurement strategy best described as strategic incoherence. Coal, palm oil, nickel, and mineral fuels dominate the export basket. Buying simultaneously from the US, South Korea, France, Turkey, Netherlands, and Brazil has produced a multi-dependency rather than non-alignment. The KF-21 partnership payments fell into arrears. No autonomous systems operational record. No consistent doctrine. The binding constraint of 0.5 is not a judgment — it is a description.
